title: Show, don't tell: communicate company values through actions, not marketing adjectives
summary: Jason Cohen argues that listing brand adjectives like "fast, easy, scalable, robust" destroys believability. Authentic values are demonstrated through concrete actions (return policies, answering the phone, real testimonials), and only after you walk the walk have you earned the right to call it out.

principles.text: If you have to tell people something is true, they automatically don't believe you; actions speak louder than words.
principles.quote: The cardinal rule of authenticity and believability is that actions speak louder than words. A corollary is that if you have to tell me something's true, I automatically don't believe you.

principles.text: Piling on adjectives (easy, fast, scalable, robust) makes every claim suspect, since no real product has zero trade-offs.
principles.quote: Since I don't know which of these claims are true, now I distrust them all. And you haven't communicated anything tangible. Fail.

principles.text: Values are the reason behind your actions and the consistency in how you do business, not taglines or mission statements.
principles.quote: Values are the reason for your actions, the theme behind your words, and the underlying consistency in how you do business.

principles.text: Prove quality with policy, not a promise: a no-questions-asked return policy beats saying 'your satisfaction is important to us'.
principles.quote: If you have a high-quality product, you don't say "Your satisfaction is important to us," you have a 90-day no-questions-asked return policy.

principles.text: Prove you care about customers by answering the phone and showing 100 real testimonials, not claiming '100 companies use us'.
principles.quote: If you care about talking to customers, you don't play a recorded message saying their call is important to you, you simply answer the phone.

principles.text: Once you're walking the walk, you've earned the right to call it out, as tangible demonstrations rather than trite phrases.
principles.quote: Once you're walking the walk, then you've earned the right to call it out
